21.0.s.en: (1) The birth, circumcision and weaning of Isaac

21.0.0.en: Visited: God remembered Sarah and granted her to conceive as He had promised her.

21.0.1.en: Sarah conceived as God had promised her and gave birth at the time He had set (ch. 18:10), and she and Abraham rejoiced, and they named him Isaac as God had called him.

21.0.2.en: Trust in God's promises to you, for they are faithful and true and must come to pass however adverse the surrounding circumstances, and even ask God for His promises in faith and hope for blessed eternity, and so you will rise above all pains.

21.1.0.en: Abraham took care to carry out God's word by circumcising every male, so he circumcised Isaac on the eighth day. His age at that time was a hundred years, and he rejoiced at begetting the son of promise, who was a clear and miraculous gift from God.

21.2.0.en: God has made me laugh: He has given me great joy.

21.2.1.en: All who hear will laugh with me: everyone who hears of Isaac's birth rejoices and congratulates Sarah and Abraham. Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children: people's amazement and joy at Isaac's birth and Sarah's nursing him, and their congratulations to his parents.

21.2.2.en: Sarah declared her joy at Isaac's birth and at people's congratulating her on the birth and the nursing despite the old age of herself and Abraham.

21.3.0.en: It is customary in the East that a child be weaned at about two years of age, so Isaac was weaned at this age, and Abraham rejoiced at this event, which represents Isaac's maturing, and made a feast for his loved ones and neighbors. He did not make a feast at the birth but at the weaning, out of his concern for his son's maturing.

21.4.0.en: Hagar and her son Ishmael, who was sixteen years old, were vexed when Isaac was weaned because of the great feast that was made for Isaac, whereas no feast was made for Ishmael when he was weaned; and because Hagar thought that her son was the only heir of Abraham, and now Isaac had appeared, who rivals him and may even take a larger inheritance than he because of Abraham's care for him. She passed these feelings to her son Ishmael, who began to trouble the child Isaac with mockery and scorn. The Apostle Paul describes this joking as persecution, that is, he was troubling him severely (Gal 4:29).

21.5.0.en: Sarah was greatly distressed for her child Isaac, persecuted by his older brother, and feared that he would harm him, so she told Abraham to cast out the maidservant and her son, so that Ishmael would not inherit anything of Abraham's possessions but all would be Isaac's.

21.6.0.en: Abraham was greatly displeased at Sarah's words because he loved his son Ishmael, who had become a young man, and felt that Sarah's words contained selfishness and injustice toward Ishmael.

21.7.0.en: God agreed with Sarah's words and told Abraham to listen to her voice. Even if there was in her words distress at Ishmael or injustice to him, yet on the other hand only Isaac is the son of promise, whereas Ishmael was born according to human will and not the will of God. Nevertheless God promised Abraham to bless Ishmael after he cast him out together with his mother, and to give him great offspring.

21.7.1.en: Obey God's commandments even if they are against your will or your feelings, because His wisdom surpasses all understanding and He knows your good, and what seems bad in your eyes may be the best. Know that you are not more tender toward people than He is, so accept His will in all your life.

21.8.s.en: (3) The casting out of Hagar and Ishmael

21.8.0.en: The wilderness of Beersheba: it lies on the southern border of the land of Canaan, that is, Palestine.

21.8.1.en: Abraham obeyed God as was his habit, rising above his fatherly feelings, and gave her bread, that is, food, and a skin of water, which Hagar and her son Ishmael carried on their shoulders, and they headed south toward the wilderness of Beersheba. He sent them away early, perhaps that they might reach a suitable place to stay before the day ended.

21.9.0.en: The water in the skin ran out after they had walked a long time in the desert, and Ishmael began to thirst until his strength failed. His mother feared he would die of thirst and could not bear to see him die before her eyes, so she sat him down, faint, under a tree, while she sat far from him, looking at him and watching him, and praying and weeping to God to rescue her and her son. Ishmael could not raise his voice in weeping because of his weakness from thirst, but his heart was asking God to rescue him without speaking, or perhaps he was whispering a few words. A bowshot: the average distance an arrow travels from the one who shoots it to the place it reaches when shot from the bow, a distance that is not small but within sight.

21.10.0.en: Hold him with your hand: support him and take courage.

21.10.1.en: Hagar heard the voice of an angel speaking to her from heaven, and perhaps she saw him in a beautiful form or a great light, and he reassured her that God had heard Ishmael's prayers, which came from his heart or in faint whispers he raised to heaven while he lay under the tree, for Ishmael had learned much about God from his father Abraham. He informed her that God would keep him and bless him, and even give him many offspring, so that he would become a nation great in number.

21.11.0.en: God guided her to a well that was near her, which perhaps had been hidden behind some trees, so she saw it and hurried to it to fill the skin from it and give her thirsty son to drink, so that he regained his strength, and she also drank with him, and they were strengthened and continued their journey.

21.12.0.en: An archer: a hunter of animals.

21.12.1.en: The wilderness of Paran: it lies north of Sinai.

21.12.2.en: Hagar and her son Ishmael reached the wilderness of Paran and lived there, and her son learned to hunt animals, and she chose for him a wife from Egypt, of her own race, so he married and settled in the north of Sinai.

21.12.3.en: God hears your prayer, especially in distress, when it comes from your heart, for He is near you and rescues you and strengthens you however weak you are, and solves your problems however impossible they seem. So accustom yourself to take refuge in Him every day in your various needs.

21.13.s.en: (4) The treaty of Abraham and Abimelech

21.13.0.en: Phichol: that is, the mouth of all, and it was probably the title of the commander of the army, who was considered as the prime minister, next to the king directly.

21.13.1.en: Abimelech sensed Abraham's success and the blessing of God that was with him during his stay in Gerar, so he feared his power and asked to make a treaty of safety between himself and Abraham so that he would not harm him; and he reminded him of his kindness to him, as he had welcomed him in his land and he had lived in peace throughout the previous period. Abraham agreed to make the treaty and to swear not to expose him to harm or wrong him.

21.13.2.en: God gives awe and favor to His children in the eyes of those around them, so do not fear those around you, but hold fast to God's commandments and live a life of repentance, and He will bless you and keep you and make those around you hold you in awe, for they feel the power of God that is in you, even if you are quiet and silent.

21.14.0.en: Abraham reproached Abimelech about a well that he had dug and that Abimelech's servants had seized, and Abimelech apologized to Abraham because he had not known of this wrong and wished that Abraham had told him so that he could have prevented it. From this appear Abraham's strength and Abimelech's gentleness, respect and fear of Abraham, and it also appears that the spiritual person has the right to demand his rights as long as this does not cause problems and clashes that make him lose his peace.

21.15.0.en: Abraham welcomed Abimelech's visit and his request for a treaty and offered him gifts of sheep and oxen, and they swore not to wrong each other and made the treaty.

21.16.0.en: Abraham set seven ewe lambs aside and Abimelech noticed that and asked him about them, and Abraham said to him, this is another gift I offer you to establish my ownership of this well that was before them, a well that Abraham had dug. Abimelech accepted it, and this was wisdom on Abraham's part, for he established his ownership in a gentle way, and for this reason this well was called "Beersheba," in reference to the seven ewe lambs. Then Abimelech departed and returned to his country (map 6).

21.17.0.en: A tamarisk tree: tall trees with strong wood and thread-like leaves, regarded as windbreaks, planted around a place to enclose it and protect it from the sands.

21.17.1.en: Everlasting: eternal and without beginning, that is, lasting without beginning or end.

21.17.2.en: Abraham planted tamarisk trees, and this was a declaration of his settling in this place, and he built an altar to God and offered sacrifices and prayers, so he blessed the place and lived in it, in the south of the land of Canaan, for a long time.

22.0.0.en: After God had appeared to Abraham many times and confirmed His promises of blessing to him, and after He had given him Isaac, the son of promise, and had blessed his possessions and strength when he defeated Chedorlaomer, so that a strong friendship arose between him and God, He appeared to him this time to test him, to bring out his virtues and increase him in love. This is of course different from the temptations that Satan devises to make us fall into sin.

22.1.0.en: Your son, your only son: Isaac became Abraham's only son after the sending away of Ishmael, and he was a young man; the Fathers expect that his age was not less than 25 years, and some say that he had passed thirty.

22.1.1.en: Whom you love: because he was the son of his old age and in him all the divine promises of blessing are fulfilled.

22.1.2.en: The land of Moriah: its meaning is teacher, or vision, or the Lord provides, because there God taught Abraham self-giving love, and Abraham saw God, and He spoke with him, and God prepared a ransom for his son. It is said that it lies east of Jerusalem, at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, where David built an altar and God stopped the plague (2 Sam 24:24), and there also Solomon built the temple. There is another opinion that it lies north of Jerusalem, where Mount Gerizim is, and it is said that Golgotha was in the land of Moriah.

22.1.3.en: God asked Abraham for an exceedingly hard thing, that he offer Isaac, his only son, so greatly beloved to him, as a sacrifice to God, and go to the land of Moriah, and there He would guide him to a mountain to go up on and offer Isaac as a sacrifice there.

22.1.4.en: If a commandment seems hard to you, do not be troubled, for God will give you help to fulfil it, and in carrying it out your love for God appears, your faith grows and you receive countless blessings.

22.2.s.en: (2) The way to offering the sacrifice

22.2.0.en: Split wood: that is, he prepared it to burn quickly and arranged it as sticks suitable for burning.

22.2.1.en: God appeared to Abraham in Beersheba by night, and Abraham rose early and prepared the wood with which he would kindle the burnt offering, that is, his son whom he would slaughter, and here his immediate obedience to God appears. He did not tell Sarah lest she hinder him by her motherly feelings from carrying out God's command. He took with him two young men of his servants to carry water and food for the journey, rode a donkey and went on the road toward the land of Moriah, that is, toward Jerusalem, with Isaac his son.

22.3.0.en: Abraham walked with Isaac from Beersheba to Jerusalem for three days, and when he reached the land of Moriah God guided him to the mountain on which Isaac would be offered, so he told his two young men, his young servants who had come with him, to sit at the foot of the mountain with the donkey while he and his son Isaac went up the mountain to offer a sacrifice and then return to them. This proves Abraham's faith in God's power to raise his son after he slaughtered him, so that he would return with him and meet the two young men.

22.4.0.en: Isaac, the young man over twenty-five years of age, carried the wood of the burnt offering, as Christ carried His cross, while Abraham held the fire and the knife, and the two of them walked together going up the mountain.

22.5.0.en: Isaac wondered, as he walked with his father Abraham to offer a burnt offering to God, that there was no animal with them to slaughter, so he asked his father about the animal that they would slaughter. This was a very painful question to the heart of Abraham, the tender father, but his faith in God and reliance on Him made him hold himself together and answer his son with reassuring words, that God who commanded us to offer a sacrifice to Him will Himself prepare for us the sacrifice that we shall offer. So Isaac fell silent and walked with his father.

22.5.1.en: If some questions from those around you wound your feelings or stir your emotions, do not doubt your faith in God's commandments, and bear the pains for His name's sake, and you will receive God's great blessings.

22.6.0.en: Abraham told his son Isaac that he would be the sacrifice offered to God as He had commanded, and Isaac submitted and obeyed although he was a young man able to resist an aged old man like his father Abraham, and in this he is a type of Christ, who emptied Himself and obeyed unto death by His own will. So Abraham built an altar with the help of Isaac his son, arranged the wood on it, bound Isaac and laid him on the wood ... How painful this was to the heart of Abraham, the father and the old man, but for God's sake he obeyed and raised the knife to slay Isaac.

22.6.1.en: Trust that God seeks your good and cannot harm you, so obey His commandments however heavy they seem and He will support you to fulfil them, and by this you show your love for Him, experience Him and enjoy a rest and joy that surpass all understanding. Slay your own will so that you may enjoy the will of God.

22.7.0.en: At the decisive moment, before the knife came near Isaac, the angel of God appeared and called to Abraham and prevented him from bringing the knife near Isaac, and praised him that he feared God and loved Him to the degree of offering Him the dearest thing he had, his only son, in whom he would receive the promises. When it says of God "Now I know," it does not mean that He did not know before, but He expresses Himself in a way we understand as human beings, declaring Abraham's righteousness before all generations; He means, now Abraham's righteousness has appeared.

22.8.0.en: God directed Abraham's sight, and he looked behind him and found a ram caught by its horns in one of the trees, which God had prepared, and He commanded him to offer it as a sacrifice in place of Isaac, so Abraham slaughtered it and offered it as a burnt offering before God. By this Isaac is a type of Christ the Redeemer in the following:

22.8.1.en: 1- Isaac carried the burnt offering as Christ carried the cross on the way to Golgotha.

22.8.2.en: 2- Isaac was bound and laid on the wood as Christ was bound and hung on the cross.

22.8.3.en: 3- The knife was raised to slay Isaac as Christ died and was slain on the cross.

22.8.4.en: 4- Isaac returned alive after the ram was offered in his place as Christ rose on the third day.

22.8.5.en: 5- The offering of Isaac showed Abraham's love and great sacrifice and Isaac's submission and love for God, as the cross showed the love of the Father and the submission of the Son.

22.8.6.en: 6- Isaac used to go out into the field in the evening to meditate (ch. 24:63), and Christ used to withdraw to pray.

22.9.0.en: Abraham rejoiced at the rescue of his son Isaac from death and at seeing God and experiencing His fatherhood and tenderness, so he called the name of this place Jehovah-jireh, that is, he saw God in this place, and this expression became a proverb said in all the following generations of everyone who relies on God and obeys His word, of whom it is said that he has seen God and experienced Him.

22.10.0.en: After God had prevented Abraham from slaying his son and given him the ram in his place, He called to him a second time from heaven by His angel, renewing the covenant with him clearly because of his surpassing love in accepting to offer Isaac as a sacrifice to God.

22.11.0.en: God renewed His covenant to Abraham and promised him the following:

22.11.1.en: 1- He gives him a great blessing in his spiritual and material life.

22.11.2.en: 2- He multiplies his seed greatly although he now has only one son.

22.11.3.en: 3- He gives strength to his seed so that they overcome their enemies. What is meant by the gate is the entrance of the city, for every city has a gate and whoever storms it can gain dominion over it. This happened in the victory of the children of Israel over the peoples who lived in the land of Canaan by the hand of Joshua, and then appeared even more in Christ's victory over Satan and his binding by the cross.

22.11.4.en: 4- The seed of Abraham, that is, Christ, since He did not say seeds, in whom is the salvation of mankind that believes in Him.

22.12.0.en: Abraham came down from the mountain with Isaac and found the two young men, his servants, waiting for him, and he returned riding his donkey to Beersheba, where he lived, a distance of three days, which signifies Christ's Resurrection after three days. Beersheba also signifies Baptism, which is the entrance to the Mysteries and which the believer receives from the blood of Christ, slain on the cross, as the sacrifice was offered on the mountain.

22.12.1.en: God's blessings to you are very abundant if you respond to His love, for He is rich and at the same time a tender Father who wants to give you much ... only rely on Him and do not be troubled by the circumstances of the turbulent world, and hold fast to His commandments, and He gives you a blessing and strength that remain with you forever.
